tests.mutation: In a throwaway copy, net10.0 suite run; InitiativeRules.Order ranked lowest first (`.OrderBy(c => c.Initiative)`); this test went red. It went red too when TurnOrder.TurnsInRound reversed the order in even rounds, and when a tie break was demanded where there was no tie (`assignments.IsEmpty && assignments.Length > 99`).

In a throwaway copy, net10.0 suite run; InitiativeRules.Order ignored the stated tie breaks, keeping tied combatants in listing order (`.ThenBy(c => 0)`); this test went red, and so did the seeded replay. It went red too under the ascending-order mutation.
